result.rationale: The diff adds an unconditional fetch to https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token inside the SalesforceCalendarService setup (the block ending with `return new jsforce.Connection(...)`), with no expiry check anywhere in the added code. Previously the constructor did not refresh tokens. Now every instantiation of the service performs a token refresh, which can rotate/invalidate refresh tokens and rate-limit the endpoint. The mechanism (unconditional refresh on each connection creation) is verifiable in the diff; the severity depends on call frequency, which is not fully visible.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new code fetches `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` using the stored `refresh_token` and updates the credential in the DB every time the service/connection code path runs (it happens immediately after `const credentialKey = credential.key ...`, with no expiry/"is expired" check). This makes refresh happen unconditionally rather than only when the access token is expired, which can cause unnecessary token refresh calls and churn; the diff does not show any guard against that.
